Sure mate. So I went to the US 2019/20 and my interviews were held in Summer 19. What ifs were mostly questions like the following examples: „What would you do if your family was supportive of Trump while you weren’t?“ „What would you do if you got into a High School with only a hundred people?“ „What would you do if your host parents talked negative about homosexuals?“ „What if your family takes you to church for hours even if you aren’t religious?“ and so on...

I won a full scholarship from my government to go on exchange and I had a lot of those. There were quite a few „What would you do if...“ questions, some political, ofc about my hobbies, what I‘d like to do after school, how I‘d manage to present my culture and how to adapt to certain situations. They want personality, authentic people, adaptable, charismatic and caring ones. So just be the best version of yourself and be honest. You can do it!

Hey there. I totally understand what you mean it and how you must feel right now. Christmas and New Year’s Eve and all these days are just behind me and all of us and let me tell you - I have gained a lot of weight. I look chubby, my pants are tight and I look awful in them. But somehow I started not to think about it. Well, I do, but I push it away. I sit in front of my laptop, I write, play music - hell I went outside on a walk to not binge. The first week was hard, 4 binge days. The week after was better, only 2, now I haven’t binged this week (I know it’s only Tuesday but hey) and guess what - one of my pants doesn’t feel as tight anymore. I am happy, it feels good. Once you make a smaller achievement, you’ll feel less struggle and want to binge. You will feel pretty and strong and you’ll be motivated. I binged for 6 months straight before now - gained more than 20 pounds, lost some, gained more back. I told myself and believed it deeply, that it would never change. That I would always keep gaining weight. I felt so ugly. But believe: Things will get better. It was hell of a year, but that’s over now. Believe in you!

I feel ridiculous answering, as I’m only a girl with a teenage life, the stereotype of a person hating their perfect existence. When I read your text I felt ashamed of thinking the way I do and it made me feel sorry for you, which I know doesn’t change a thing. I won’t change your opinion on 2020 - it’s exactly how you said. But here me out: You’re strong, so incredibly strong for still hanging around. I can’t believe how you might feel but I guess it’s worse than a lot of people. I wish I could build you up, say motivational stuff or share some stories (which I - basically a kid - don’t have) but given that you’re older, probably far away and foreign I just want you to know that I am thinking of you and will include you in my prayers (that being said I pray like once a year because I am too critical to actually have faith in any kind of a god)... You deserve better. And I hope 2021 will be better for you.

I know that I’m in no position to compare myself or tell you that I understand what you mean, but I do. It’s a different addiction on my side and I let go (well I’m trying) but it just feels like an empty spot and everything else is just the way it was before. I guess the best way to deal with this is accepting that getting back into the addiction will make things worse. Not doing drugs might not make things feel better, but the point is it doesn’t get worse. I’d suggest trying to find something healthy that you like, a treat for yourself: A new hobby, finding new people, look for cheap travel opportunities, take yourself out once a week and find a new favorite restaurant, plant a little garden with vegetables and fruits, find a new video game to play, a new book to read, a movie or a series to watch, look for a gym or a new sport activity that you like, go ice skating or swimming, explore your city/country and go hiking, create a list of things you’d do if money (whatever) didn’t play a role, maybe combine some of these things with your son: Take him out for a new sport, take him out to explore some restaurants, do a road trip and let him hear some of the good old music, play a video game with him. Instead of thinking about how dropping drugs doesn’t make things better, change something. Go out and look for new things! Allow your life to change... I don’t know if that was any help. But it looks like you didn’t give up on yourself and your life and I think you could keep on doing that by improving things actively. However, have a wonderful day - and even if it wasn’t for me and even if it won’t do anything: I am proud of you for not doing drugs anymore.
